errors_A: "read-only mems currently have no index at all": the engine builds indexes via build_all(&self.store, &self.schemas) and the boot loop in engine/boot.rs inserts a schema entry for every resolved mount, read-only ones included (only quarantined mounts are skipped), so read-only mems are indexed too; only the build_all docstring says "writable".
rationale: Both correctly say there is no vector search or embedding model: no such code path exists under crates, search is a per-mem in-RAM tantivy index ranked by BM25 with schema title_weight/search_weight boosts (default schema: title 100, sections up to 40, metadata text 1.0). Binary runs confirm no stemming (schedule finds nothing, scheduler hits), diacritic folding (hauser finds Häuser), 0.5 expansion decay, proximity-ranked related_to, and warned-but-ignored unknown filters. A offers more routes (Louvain communities, NEIGHBOURHOOD_CAPPED, wasm caveat) but asserts one false fact about read-only mems. B is fully verified, gives concrete tokenizer examples, and honestly states embedding search must live outside the engine.
